source.name: Bosa Properties official website
source.sourceType: official direct property development and management company website captured in Playwright Chromium
source.rightsEvidence: Requester-attested clearance dated 2026-09-29 covers internal desktop and mobile screenshot retention, derived design prompts, and pipeline-model reference use. No source-owner grant was supplied or independently verified.

referenceDna.annotatedDescription: A concise real-estate development thesis sits over a wide urban property image and a portfolio action. A broad project surface lets a visitor filter by sector and geography before the page divides residential offerings from office, retail, industrial, and hotel portfolios. Later chapters explain the operating model and work culture, then close with career, contact, and regional subsidiary pathways. Compared with agent-oriented designs, this pattern organizes a property company as a portfolio of projects and business lines. Source buildings, prices, counts, land claims, logos, and market details are not client facts.

heroGeometry.alignment: large architectural backdrop with short statement and compact portfolio control
heroGeometry.viewport: introduce the developer's verified role and lead to a portfolio or inquiry route

navigationGeometry.placement: horizontal company menu with portfolio and solution routes
navigationGeometry.mobile: use a concise menu with visible sector paths and no narrow multi-column navigation

typography.scale: measured mission headline, clear sector headings, small project-state labels

palette.contrastIntent: corporate readability with image-first project moments and strong text contrast

imageTreatment.mode: built environment renders and finished places
imageTreatment.crop: wide development hero followed by medium project images and sector thumbnails
imageTreatment.focalPoint: keep building form and public realm visible without overlay copy obscuring architecture

servicePresentation.interaction: select an asset sector or project stage, then browse individually described developments

ctaPlacement.secondary: contact the team for leasing or partnership questions
ctaPlacement.early: portfolio exploration control in the hero

motion.library: native video or image transitions with optional GSAP sequencing
motion.reducedMotion: poster image and accessible static portfolio filters

mobileRecomposition.strategy: sector selector then vertically stacked project cards
rules: show sector choices before a long project inventory
make project names and current status readable
stack cards in a single column and avoid desktop-only hover filters
keep corporate contact and accessibility links easy to reach

prohibitedPatterns: copying Bosa name, wordmark, project names, renderings, property facts, statistics, or public claims
inventing completed units, development totals, managed square footage, or environmental targets
presenting an active project as delivered without client confirmation
using residential property imagery as proof of client ownership
flattening distinct property sectors into repeated generic service cards

requiredSignatureElements.description: Portfolio browsing distinguishes asset sectors or project stages before showing results.
The main content has a real project inventory with client-verified project status and context.
A separate company-purpose chapter explains the relationship between development and property operations.

acceptanceChecks: The page identifies the client's actual role as developer, operator, landlord, or broker.
Portfolio filters reflect only services and projects confirmed by the client.
Current project status is clear and not inferred from imagery.
Mobile sector and project browsing remains keyboard and touch accessible.
No unsupplied development, sustainability, scale, or results claim appears.

review.notes: Official homepage and About page identify property development and management activities, residential and commercial sectors, project portfolio, and contact details. Full-page desktop and mobile captures were inspected. The only broken image diagnostic was a non-content Bing tracking pixel; seven to eight lazy content image elements remained unresolved at capture time.
